correctness.rationale: Use the initial orthogonal singular-vector pairs with signed coefficients y, even for repeated singular values; the partial polar factor acts by sign(y), with sign(0)=0, in these pairs. For q>0 the post-step positive radii follow |qs−τ|, and the reverse triangle inequality gives contraction to δ=τ/(1+q) for every mode that stays nonzero. Zero is absorbing and is not governed by the positive-radius formula. More explicitly the first positive zero preimage is τ/q>τ, and every radius >τ has exactly one positive preimage (radius+τ)/q. The exceptional radii are therefore τ∑_(i=1)^j q^−i, j≥1. All surviving radii eventually satisfy qs<τ; then the post signed modes flip for α>0 and preserve sign for α<0, yielding the stated antipodal limits or the fixed matrix. Pre equals post for α>0. For α<0 pre always flips on nonzero modes and has radial map qs+τ, converging to τ/(1−q). In the nonresonant rank-r comparison the Frobenius factors √r cancel, giving ηa/(2−ηa); the post objective is 3rλ²/(2a) when α<0. The critical step has post zero and pre an exact cycle after one step. The prox radii decrease by at least τ while positive, so they hit the unique minimizer in finitely many steps. The normalized nonzero spectrum becomes uniform on the surviving rank, proving the effective-rank assertion. The nonzero rank-r and Frobenius-ratio claims are read with the nonresonance condition in Finding and Limitations (not for every positive-rank initialization); for example α=−1/2, τ=1, y₀=2 gives post zero and pre nonzero.
residual_risks: The frozen numerical SVD diagnostic uses a tolerance and does not check the exact resonant set; exact arithmetic and the proof address that boundary. For resonant initial data replace r by the surviving rank in post limits, or by zero if every mode dies. No extension to generic nonisotropic or approximate-polar training follows.

value.rationale: The comparison is a motivated counterbenchmark for reading an additive polar correction as rank reduction or a proximal step, and for reading a one-step order bound as long-run robustness. Above the critical step the two methods exhibit qualitatively different matrix attractors, with an exact dimension-independent nonresonant ratio that diverges at the stability boundary. That comparative result is the useful contribution, not textbook proximal thresholding by itself.
residual_risks: This is an ideal centered-quadratic counterbenchmark, not evidence about the magnitude of rank reduction or performance in neural-network settings.
